an aggregate of five sacred fires; i. e. (अन्वाहार्यपचन or
 दक्षिण, गार्हपत्य, आहवनीय, सभ्य, and आवसथ्य).
a householder who maintains the five sacred fires; पञ्चाग्नयो धृतव्रताः

five mystic fires supposed to exist in the body; तेजो ह्यग्निस्तथा
 क्रोधश्चक्षुरूष्मा तथैव च । अग्निर्जरयते यच्च पञ्चाग्नेयाः शरीरिणः ॥

one who is acquainted with the doctrine of these fires. ˚साधनम्
 four fires on four sides and the sun above the head. This is a form of penance.

+ -अङ्ग a. five-membered, having five parts or divisions as
 in पञ्चाङ्गः प्रणामः (i. e. बाहुभ्यां चैव जानुभ्यां शिरसा वक्षसा
 दृशा); कृतपत्र्चाङ्गविनिर्णयो नयः

(see Malli. and Kām.

a kind of horse with five spots in different parts of his body.
collection or aggregate of five parts.

five modes of devotion (silent prayer, oblations, libations, bathing
 idols and feeding Brāhmaṇas)

the five parts of a tree; त्वक्पत्रकुसुमं मूलफलमेकस्य शाखिनः ।
 एकत्र मिलितं चैतत् पञ्चाङ्गमिति संज्ञितम् ॥

a calendar or almanac, so called because it treats of five things:−
 (तिथिर्वारश्च नक्षत्रं योगः करणमेव च); चतुरङ्गबलो राजा
 जगतीं वशमानयेत् । अहं पञ्चाङ्गबलवानाकाशं वशमानये ॥ Subhāṣ.
 ˚गुप्तः a turtle. ˚पत्रम् a calendar. ˚विनिर्णयः the five
 rules are as follows; सहायाः साधनोपाया विभागो देशकालयोः । विनिपातप्रतीकारः
 सिद्धिः पञ्चाङ्गमिष्यते ॥ Kām.; cf.

 the propitiousness or favourable state of five important points; i. e.
 तिथि, वार, नक्षत्र, योग, and करण (in astrology).

 measuring five fingers.
+ -अजम्, -आजम् the five products of the goat; cf. पञ्चगव्य.
+ -अजम्, -आजम् the five products of the goat; cf. पञ्चगव्य.

+ -अप्सरस् n. N. of a lake, said to have been created by the

+ -अमरा The five plants i. e. (Mar. भांग, दूर्वा, बेल, निर्गुडी
 and तुळस.

the aggregate of five drugs: dry ginger, a species of Moon-seed (Cocculus
 cordifolius, Mar. गुळवेल), Asparagus racemosus (Mar. शतावरी),
 Hypoxis brevifolia
[]

the collection of five sweet things used in worshipping deities; (दुग्धं
 च शर्करा चैव घृतं दधि तथा मधु).

+ -अम्लम् the aggregate of five acid plants (the jujube, pomegranate,
 sorrel, spondias and citron).

+ -अवयव a. five-membered (as a syllogism, the five members
 being, प्रतिज्ञा, हेतु, उदाहरण, उपनय and निगमन q. v.).

+ -अवस्थः a corpse (so called because it is resolved into the five
 elements) cf. पञ्चत्व below.
+ -अविकम् the five products of the sheep; cf. पञ्चगव्य.

+ -आतप a. doing penance with five fires (i. e. with four
 fires and the sun); cf.
+ -आत्मक a. consisting of five elements (as body).

+ -आम्नायाः m. (pl.) five Śāstras supposed to have proceeded
 from the five mouths of Śiva.

+ -आयतनी, -आयतनम् a group of five deities like गणपति, विष्णु,
 शंकर, देवी and सूर्य.

+ -आयतनी, -आयतनम् a group of five deities like गणपति, विष्णु,
 शंकर, देवी and सूर्य.

+ -इन्द्रियम् an aggregate of the five organs (of sense or actions;
 see इन्द्रियम्).

+ -इषुः, -बाणः, -शरः epithets of the god of love; (so called

 च नवमल्लिका । नीलोत्पलं च पञ्चैते पञ्चबाणस्य सायकाः ॥ the five
 arrows are also thus named:− संमोहनोन्मादनौ च शोषणस्तापनस्तथा ।
 स्तम्भनश्चेति कामस्य पञ्चबाणाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥).

+ -उपचारः the five articles of worship i. e. (गन्ध, पुष्प,
 धूप, दीप and नैवेद्य).
+ -उष्मन् m. (pl.) the five digestive fires supposed to be in the body.
+ -कपाल a. prepared or offered in five cups.
Relating to an oblation offered in five cups (कपाल);

+ -कर्ण a. branded in the ear with the number ‘five’ (as cattle
 &c.); cf.

+ -कर्मन् n. (in medicine) the five kinds of treatment; i. e.
 1 वमन ‘giving emetics’; 2 रेचन ‘purging’; 3 नस्य
 ‘giving strenutatories’; 4 अनुवासन ‘administering an enema which is oily’
, and 5 निरूह ‘administering an enema which is not oily’.
 वमनं रेचनं नस्यं निरूहश्चानुवासनम् । पञ्चकर्मेदमन्यच्च ज्ञेयमुत्क्षेपणादिकम् ॥.
+ -कल्याणकः a horse with white feet and a white mouth.

+ -कषाय a decoction from the fruits of five plants (जम्बु, शाल्मलि,
 वाट्याल, बकुल and बदर).

+ -कृत्यम् the five actions by which the Supreme Power manifests
 itself (सृष्टि, स्थिति, संहार, तिरोभाव and अनुग्रहकरण).

+ -कृष्णः + .({@-ष्णाः@}) The five deities of Mahānubhāva sect namely चक्रवर्ती
 कृष्ण, Datta of Mātāpura, Gundam Raul of ऋद्धिपुर, चांगदेव राऊळ
 of द्वारावती and चांगदेव राऊळ of प्रतिष्ठान.

+ -कोलम् the five spices taken collectively; पिप्पली पिप्पलीमूलं
 चव्यचित्रकनागरम् । पञ्चकोलं … … … (Mar. पिंपळी, पिंपळमूळ,
 चवक, चित्रक ब सुंठ).

+ -कोषाः m. (pl.) the five vestures or wrappers supposed to
 invest the soul; they are:− अन्नमयकोष or the earthly body
[]
 (स्थूलशरीर); प्राणमयकोष the vesture of the vital airs; मनोमयकोष
 the sensorial vesture; विज्ञानमयकोष the cognitional vesture (these
 three form the लिङ्गशरीर); and आनन्दमयकोष the last vesture,
 that of beatitude. कोषैरन्नमयाद्यैः पञ्चभिरात्मा न संवृतो भाति ।
 निजशक्तिसमुत्पन्नैः शैवालपटलैरिवाम्बु वापीस्थम् ॥ Vivekacūḍāmaṇi.
+ -गत a. (in alg.) raised to the fifth power.

+ -गव्यम् the five products of the cow taken collectively; i. e.
 milk, curds, clarified butter or ghee, urine, and cowdung (क्षीरं
 दधि तथा चाज्यं मूत्रं गोमयमेव च).

+ -गुण + .({@-णाः@}) the five objects of sense (रूप, रस, गन्ध, स्पर्श
 and शब्द).
a tortoise (as drawing in its 4 feet and head).
the materialistic system of philosophy, the doctrines of the Cārvākas.

+ -चामरम् N. of 2 kinds of metre; प्रमाणिकापदद्वयं वदन्ति

N. of a demon who had assumed the form of a conch-shell, and was slain

 and pitṛs; यस्मिन् पञ्च पञ्चजना आकाशश्च प्रतिष्ठितः Bṛ.

 two senses); (for a full exposition see Śārīrabhāṣya on Br. Sūtras
+ -जनीन a. devoted to the five races.

an epithet of Buddha as possessing the five kinds of knowledge.
a man familiar with the doctrines of the Pāśupatas.

the five elements taken collectively; i. e. पृथ्वी, अप्, तेजस्,

 मांस, मत्स्य, मुद्रा and मैथुन.

 रस, स्पर्श, रूप and गन्ध).

+ -दशिन् a. made or consisting of fifteen.
